title: Angular 21 & 22 complete feature deep dive
exp: Angular 21 (Nov 2025) and Angular 22 (June 2026, current) represent the culmination of the signal-first direction. Being able to discuss specific features in detail — not just 'signals and zoneless' — is the real differentiator at senior level.
pts: **Angular 21 (Nov 20, 2025):** zoneless default for new projects; Signal Forms experimental; Vitest replaces Karma; Angular ARIA headless components (dev preview)

**Angular 22 (June 3, 2026):** OnPush default for new projects; Signal Forms stable; Resource API (`resource`, `rxResource`, `httpResource`) stable; Angular ARIA stable; TypeScript 6 support; improved SSR/hydration

**Signal Forms (v22 stable):** `signalForm({ email: '' })` — form value is a signal (`form.value()`); no valueChanges Observable needed; integrates natively with OnPush/zoneless; custom validators return signals

**`resource()` API:** generic reactive data-fetching — define a loader function, resource tracks when its signal inputs change and re-fetches. `resource.value()`, `.status()`, `.error()`, `.reload()` are all signals
**`rxResource()`:** same as resource but the loader returns an Observable (for RxJS operators, retries, etc.) — bridges RxJS and signals
**`httpResource()`:** convenience wrapper around resource for HTTP GET — takes a URL-returning function; uses Angular's HttpClient under the hood
**Angular ARIA (v22 stable):** accessible headless component primitives (listbox, combobox, tree, menu) via CDK — unstyled, accessible, for building design systems
**TypeScript 6 support:** `using` and `await using` keywords for explicit resource cleanup; template literal improvements; no TS 5 features dropped
**Hydration improvements:** deferrable views now work with SSR hydration; partial hydration for @defer blocks — server renders @placeholder, client hydrates deferred content
pr: Convert a component that uses HttpClient + switchMap to use httpResource()
Read the Angular 22 release notes and identify one feature not covered in this lesson

qa.q: What are the key differences between Angular 21 and Angular 22?
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** Angular 21 (Nov 2025): zoneless change detection became the default for new projects; Vitest replaced Karma as the default test runner; Signal Forms shipped as experimental; Angular ARIA headless components reached developer preview. Angular 22 (June 2026): OnPush became the default change detection strategy for new components; Signal Forms and the Resource API (resource, rxResource, httpResource) were promoted to stable; Angular ARIA stabilised; TypeScript 6 support added. The through-line: Angular 22 stabilised what Angular 21 made experimental.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** T-SQL engine parses, compiles into execution plans, caches them in the plan cache, and executes via the storage engine (buffer pool & latching).

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Parameter sniffing and missing stats cause sub-optimal plan compilation, resulting in full table scans and high CPU.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** Parameterization improves plan reuse, but recompile hints (OPTION RECOMPILE) may be needed for skewed data distributions.

qa.q: What is the Resource API and what problem does it solve?
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** The Resource API (resource, rxResource, httpResource) is a signal-native data-fetching primitive. Problem solved: combining signals and async data fetching previously required converting between Observables and signals (toSignal + switchMap) or manual effect() with HTTP calls. resource()/httpResource() provides a clean abstraction: define a reactive request (function of signals), provide a loader (Promise or Observable), and get back value(), status(), isLoading(), error(), and reload() as signals — no subscribe, no async pipe, no takeUntilDestroyed.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** Signals build a fine-grained reactive dependency graph. When a signal value changes, only dependent view nodes are scheduled for DOM updating.

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Mutating signal values inside effects without untracked() causes infinite change detection loops and browser freeze.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** Signals provide predictable synchronous reactivity without Zone.js overhead, but require adapting existing RxJS-heavy codebases.

qa.q: What is the difference between resource(), rxResource(), and httpResource()?
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** resource(): generic, loader returns a Promise — use when you have any async data source (fetch, IndexedDB, WebSocket). rxResource(): loader returns an Observable — use when you need RxJS operators like retry, catchError, or debounce. httpResource(): convenience wrapper that takes a URL function and uses Angular's HttpClient under the hood — use for simple HTTP GET requests that should re-fetch when route params change. All three return the same interface: value(), isLoading(), error(), status(), reload() signals.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** Indexes store data in B-Tree structures. Clustered indexes dictate physical row storage on disk leaf pages; non-clustered indexes point to clustered keys or RIDs.

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Over-indexing degrades write performance on INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE operations and leads to index fragmentation and page splits.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** Covering indexes eliminate costly Key Lookups for read-heavy workloads but increase storage footprint and write transaction overhead.

qa.q: What does it mean that OnPush is now the default in Angular 22?
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** ng generate component now produces components with ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush without needing to specify it. This is a significant shift: new Angular apps are fully OnPush-first by default. Combined with zoneless being the default (Angular 21), and signal inputs providing the primary way to pass data, Angular 22 apps are inherently more performant and explicit about reactivity than pre-v21 apps. Existing components still need explicit OnPush — the default only applies to newly generated components in projects on Angular 22+.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** Signals build a fine-grained reactive dependency graph. When a signal value changes, only dependent view nodes are scheduled for DOM updating.

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Mutating signal values inside effects without untracked() causes infinite change detection loops and browser freeze.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** Signals provide predictable synchronous reactivity without Zone.js overhead, but require adapting existing RxJS-heavy codebases.

qa.q: What is Angular ARIA and why is it significant?
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** Angular ARIA (stable in Angular 22) is a set of accessible, unstyled headless component primitives from the CDK team — listbox, combobox, tree, menu, dialog, and more. "Headless" means they provide behaviour and accessibility (keyboard navigation, ARIA attributes, focus management) without any visual styling, so design systems can style them freely. Significance: building accessible components from scratch is extremely difficult; Angular ARIA provides the accessibility foundation so component library authors focus on styling rather than ARIA/keyboard handling.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** Parameterization improves plan reuse, but recompile hints (OPTION RECOMPILE) may be needed for skewed data distributions.
